reproduced_baseline.key_failure: Four largely repeated still-source scenes held for roughly 15 seconds each passed the old truth contract.

root_causes: FAST fallback planning deliberately reduced long-form videos up to 120 seconds to four scenes.
The FAST scene renderer used a 640x360 intermediate before upscaling to 1280x720 and encoded at 18 fps.
The truth gate accepted the four distinct source files without checking the temporal motion-source coverage of the launch profile.
The FAST mix used fixed volume multipliers but no post-mix loudness normalization; the inspected export was extremely quiet.
corrective_changes: Long-form 45-120 second output receives eight planned and rendered scenes; normal 60-second launch output has an eight-scene floor.

Launch profile uses scene-specific Pexels motion clips with item-page URLs, creator names, and Pexels license evidence; source bytes are decoded, hashed, checked for relevance, and prevented from duplicating a prior scene.

Launch truth requires eight source-motion assets with source URL, license URL and source-specific rights passing the existing rights gate; still-image animation alone cannot satisfy the motion contract.
FAST renders now process at delivery dimensions at 24 fps, use less destructive encoding settings, tag BT.709 SDR color metadata and normalize the final speech/music/effects mix.
Independent media QC measures integrated loudness and makes out-of-range audio a release-blocking failure.
Regressions preserve the previously failing four-scene launch brief as a negative benchmark.
verification: Pending CI execution on the new candidate SHA; none of these fixes are considered verified until the focused tests, full acceptance run, actual rendered source-motion records, frame/audio inspection, and truth-gate negative benchmark complete.
